title: The best-known hadith collections
intro: How the hadiths of the Prophet (SAW) were written down, checked and gathered into the six great collections.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Allah (SWT) gave the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) the task of passing on the Qur’an and explaining it: We have sent down the Book to you only so that you may make clear to them what they differed about. <small>(Qur’an, An-Nahl 16:64)</small>
So the Prophet (SAW) worked hard to explain to his Companions, in the best way, the rules in Allah’s Book. To understand the faith, the Companions stayed close to him and listened to what he said.

items: At the start of his mission, the Prophet (SAW) did not allow hadiths to be written, so that the text of the Qur’an would not get mixed with hadiths. In that time the Companions memorised what he said and did and passed it on by word of mouth.
Later the Prophet (SAW) allowed hadiths to be written, so the first hadiths were written down already in his lifetime.

Writing continued after he passed away – especially once some people began to make up hadiths on purpose. So the scholars of hadith (muhaddithun) gathered them very carefully into collections. They wrote down everything connected with the Prophet’s life, with special care for his sayings – the hadiths.

Knowing how important hadiths are, the muhaddithun spared no time or effort: they travelled to faraway places to check whether one hadith was authentic. They paid special attention to the sanad (chain of narrators): if even one narrator was unreliable, the hadith was not recorded, or it was marked as weak (da‘if).

The richest time of collecting hadiths was the end of the first and the beginning of the second century after the Hijrah. A great Islamic science grew up whose aim was to collect hadiths, select the authentic ones and arrange them by topic.

learn.html: The best-known and most authentic hadith collections are Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim. After them in authenticity come the Sunan of Abu Dawud, the Sunan of At-Tirmidhi, the Sunan of An-Nasa’i and the Sunan of Ibn Majah. Together these are called Al-Kutub as-Sittah – “the six books”. Another important collection is the Muwatta’ of Imam Malik.

learn.title: 🔎 Very careful work
learn.html: Imam Al-Bukhari at first gathered about 600,000 hadiths, and Imam Muslim about 300,000. After checking them, Al-Bukhari put about 7,000 into his Sahih, and Muslim about 12,000.

In the last decades of the 20th century and the beginning of the 21st, all of these hadith collections were translated into Bosnian by groups of scholars and by individual muhaddithun, among them Hasan-ef. Škapura, Prof. Mahmut-ef. Karalić and Prof. Dr. Šefik Kurdić.

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: The sanad is the chain of named narrators of a hadith, reaching back to the Companions who heard it from the Prophet (SAW) and remembered it. The rules for a correct sanad are very strict, so the authenticity of hadiths has been kept to this day. By authenticity, hadiths are divided into sahih – authentic, hasan – good, and da‘if – weak.

questions.q: Why did the Prophet (SAW) at first not allow hadiths to be written?
options: So they would not get mixed with the Qur’an
The chain of narrators of a hadith

questions.q: What are the six best-known collections called together?
Which two collections are the most authentic?
options: Sunan Abu Dawud and Sunan Ibn Majah

questions.q: About how many hadiths did Al-Bukhari put into his Sahih?
When was the richest time of collecting hadiths?
options: End of the 1st and start of the 2nd century after the Hijrah
